payload.title: Cabinet adopted the updated scheme, and turned down Scrutiny's request
payload.summary: Cabinet met on 11 February 2026 and, as item 12, “RESOLVED to agree the adoption of the updated Home Options policy.” All five proposed changes went through. The one thing Scrutiny had asked for did not. The report records that the recommendation to remove section 3.8.7.3 “has been considered by the Portfolio Holder but is not accepted”, and the Cabinet member for housing told the meeting that these are households who “made an active choice to move to a property without a garden”.
detail: An applicant now has to have lived in Norwich for two years to join the register, rather than six months, with the exceptions set out in law still applying.

An applicant may now turn down three offers rather than five before the application is reviewed and may be cancelled for a year. People the council owes a homelessness duty still get a single offer, as the law requires.

Two other concerns raised in the consultation were answered rather than acted on. The report says that people without a local connection staying longer in hostels is covered by the council's hostel move-on agreement, and that prioritising veterans follows the Armed Forces Covenant, which the council has signed.

Cabinet pointed families in a flat with no garden towards swapping homes with another tenant instead, and gave a figure for how often that works — “in 2025 alone, 160 council tenant households were able to move through this process”.
